newsitem.title: USA: Judge suspends Marvel disclosure hearing.
newsitem.headline: Judge suspends Marvel disclosure hearing.

text.p: A Bankruptcy Judge on Tuesday suspended a hearing on the adequacy of Marvel Entertainment Group Inc's disclosure statement after shareholders called for an adjournment.

But U.S. Bankruptcy Court Judge Helen Balick said she will let stand a March 7 date scheduled for a confirmation hearing on the company's reorganization plan for emerging from bankruptcy protection. The plan contemplates the purchase by Ronald Perelman of 420 million shares of Marvel for $365 million or $0.85 a share.

Balick explained her decision to suspend Tuesday's hearing by saying there had be inadequate notice to creditors of the disclosure statement, and that time was needed for a committee of equity-holders to be organize and to meet.

Perelman, who controls a majority stake in Marvel, has been battling with Marvel bondholders, including financier Carl Icahn. The bondholders objected to Perelman's request that they waive certain restsrictions contained in the bonds and support his plan to buy newly issued shares of Marvel at a steep discount to the market price. The company then filed for Chapter 11 on December 27, 1996.

Balick declined a request by shareholders that she appoint an examiner and told attorneys on all sides to set up a conference telephone call by the second half of next week to see "how we're progressing."
In a disclosure hearing, creditors are provided with a detailed financial accounting so they can pass an inform vote on the company's reorganization plan.
